blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Sunday told protesters not to “tarnish” the country’s reputation amid reports of police arrests and their purported “attacks” during the demonstrations in Liwasang Bonifacio while Manila hosts the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit. READ: Protesters, police clash in Manila during Asean Summit protest “At this time, we should stand united. Let’s not tarnish the image of the Philippines before the international community,” Palace Press Office Claire Castro said in Filipino during a press conference at the International Media Center in the World Trade Center.“For now, let us refrain from creating issues,” she added. “Matters like these can be […]...
